title: Fit a new toilet flapper: both rubber ears over the overflow tube's pegs, seated, chain clipped with 10-20 mm slack
instruction: Fit the new flapper and hook up its chain so that the toilet flushes and doesn't run, then let go.
context: Flappers are changed by building maintenance technicians in apartments and hotels (BLS May 2023: 303,120 Maintenance and Repair Workers, General, 49-9071, work in real estate and 86,170 in hotels) and by plumbers (O*NET 47-2152, 510,600; task "Install ... fixtures such as sinks or toilets"): together about 0.9 million. EPA WaterSense's guide for multifamily property staff says to dye-test tank toilets and "check for a tangled chain in the tank or replace a worn flapper valve"; toilets are about a quarter of water-related apartment work orders. The fix: spread each rubber ear past its peg on the overflow tube and push it on, holding the first while the second is worked, deep in a narrow tank; seat the flapper flat on the valve; clip the chain at the bead that leaves a little slack: too short holds the flapper open (the toilet runs), too long and the flush is short.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases on the table (x away from the robot, y to its left). Tank: a two-piece toilet tank (white vitreous china, walls 1 cm) with its back toward the robot (from the front the YAM's wrists would meet the tank's back wall), lid off and empty (water off), outside 20.7 x 43 cm, inside 18.7 x 41 cm and 24.5 cm deep, its back wall's outer face at x 21, centred on y 0. It stands on two 2x4 offcuts laid flat (38 mm, 25 cm long, along x at y +-12, either side of the valve shank), held to them with two ratchet straps, the offcuts clamped to the table: the tank's floor is 5 cm and its rim 29.5 cm above the table. Inside, standard parts: a 2 in flush valve (Fluidmaster 507A) centred at x 32.7, y 0 (seat ring 68 mm across, its top 3 cm above the floor); its overflow tube, 32 mm across and 21.5 cm tall, at x 27.2, y 0, with the two flapper-ear pegs (5.6 mm pins, from 31 to 44 mm either side of the tube's axis, 5.5 cm above the floor); a fill valve (32 mm shank, 6 cm float cup, top 23 cm above the floor) in the front corner on the robot's left (x 36.7, y 17), its 6 mm vinyl refill tube clipped to the overflow tube's rim, aimed down it (not pushed inside); a scoring mark on the overflow tube 13 cm above the tank floor (the lug's height when the flapper stands 60 degrees open); a right-hand trip lever (Fluidmaster 641 Perfect Fit universal lever; the model's plastic arm is 18.5 cm) whose chrome handle is on the far (front) wall at y 15, its white plastic arm 1 cm inside that wall, 20 cm above the floor, running toward the robot's right, with holes 14, 15.5 and 17 cm from the pivot; the flapper kit's stainless chain clip hangs from the middle hole. The lid lies flat on the table at x 30, y -43, its long side along x. Flapper: one new 2 in universal flapper with peg ears and a 25 cm stainless bead chain (6 mm pitch, 4.5 mm beads), the same model in every trial (Fluidmaster 502P21): black rubber seal 72 mm across with a float cup, two rubber ears on bendable arms, each with a hole that grips its peg, the chain hooked to a lug on the far edge of the seal. Start: the old flapper removed; the new one resting on the valve seat 15 mm toward the front of its fitted place, so its ears stand just in front of the pegs (mark the seal's place with a pencil line on the valve); its chain laid on the tank floor from the lug, down beside the seal at x 39, y -4, round the right of the valve to x 28.7, y -5.6, then straight toward the right-hand wall to y -16.5 (mark the path on the floor with tape).
scoring: Feeler gauge (0.5 mm), steel rule, phone photo and video, after the robot has let go and kept 3 cm clear for 1 s. 0.25 when at least one ear is on its peg (the peg through the ear's hole). 0.5 when both ears are on their pegs and the flapper is seated (seal centre within 6 mm of the valve's): the feeler enters nowhere between seal and seat. 1.0 when, besides, the chain is in the lever's clip with 10 to 20 mm of slack (pressing the handle slowly, the clip rises 10 to 20 mm before the flapper starts to lift; about two beads), and one full press of the handle (the arm turns about 40 degrees) lifts the flapper at least 60 degrees (its lug reaches the tube's mark) and it drops back seated; the trial ends at the press. 0 if the tank has moved, the flapper is torn, or the robot is within 3 cm of the flapper, chain or lever at the end.
reset_notes: About 2 minutes. Lift the chain out of the clip and leave the clip hooked in the lever's middle hole. Pull each ear back off its peg (spread it outward over the peg's tip), slide the flapper 15 mm forward on the seat to its pencil line, ears in front of the pegs, and lay the chain along its tape path on the floor. Check the refill tube is clipped to the overflow tube's rim and the handle is at rest. Replace the flapper if an ear tears or its hole has stretched loose on its peg; replace the chain clip if it no longer grips a bead.
fidelity: Tank parts rigid. Flapper: rigid seal and cup. Peg core 3 mm (real 5.6 mm pin): stable contact. Ear hole 8.5 mm, no stretch force (real push not measured): held on only when on the peg and pushed home on its boss with at least 0.5 N of contact force; easier to line up. Ear arm 1 N per 13 mm (estimate). Bead 1.5 g (real ~0.3 g): solver stability. Clip takes a bead within 8 mm for 0.3 s. Tank back-to-robot (real front-on): YAM wrists clear the far wall. Press computed. No water.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 (732 steps; 3 of 3 runs). Scripted failures: right ear left off its peg 0.25; chain clipped three beads too long (36 mm of slack) 0.5. Dream-1 run: 0.0 (valid run).
